text.TITLE: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake (after Hiroshige)
text.TASK_MD: copy the painting shown in the picture `/app/target.png` (a small acrylic painting after Utagawa Hiroshige's woodblock print Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake, 1857) onto the main sheet, **in at most 380 strokes**.
text.ENGINE_U:
at every physics step (100 Hz) the tip over a sheet is one motion event for libmypaint 1.6.1 with the
  mypaint-brushes preset `tanda/acrylic-03-paint` (dab size scaled to the paper): an opaque acrylic paint whose mark width follows the
  **pressure** (press depth / 15 mm): straight strokes at 40 mm/s are about 1.6 mm wide at a 1 mm press, 2.4 mm at 3 mm, 3.5 mm at
  5 mm, 5.2 mm at 7 mm, 7.5 mm at 9 mm, 11 mm at 11 mm and 16 mm at 13 mm; the dabs also depend on the speed and direction and carry
  the engine's own jitter (deterministic); later strokes cover earlier ones. The engine is `MyPaintPainter` in
  `/opt/tools/rcb_brush.py` (+ `/opt/mypaint`). One continuous contact is one **stroke**; paint is permanent (only `s.reset()` clears it).
text.ENGINE_L:
- Wherever the loaded tip is below a sheet's surface the brush paints an opaque acrylic mark; what the mark looks like depends on
  how you press, move and turn the brush (the practice sheet is there to find out), and later strokes cover earlier ones. One
  continuous contact of the loaded brush with the main sheet is one **stroke**. The arm is position-controlled (PD, 20 Hz targets):
  a moving target is followed with a lag.
text.SCORE_U:
- Before scoring, the main sheet is aligned with the picture: your painting is moved by the single translation (no rotation or scaling, one shift for the whole sheet, whole pixels up to 5 mm along each axis) that best matches the picture; every quantity below is taken after that shift, which is reported (`register_dx_mm`, `register_dy_mm`). If the best match lies at the 5 mm limit, no shift is applied.
- The grader compares the main sheet with the picture: both blurred (σ = 1 mm); **ΔE** = the CIELAB colour difference (ΔE*ab) per pixel over the region where either has paint (dilated by 2 mm): its mean and 90th percentile; **SSIM** of the lightness L* (σ 1.5 mm windows); **edge correlation** = the correlation of the lightness-gradient magnitudes of the two blurred pictures over that region; **paint IoU** of the painted areas (paint coverage ≥ 0.5); the **number of strokes** on the main sheet (painted contacts). **Success iff, after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, mean ΔE ≤ 2.0, p90 ΔE ≤ 6.0, SSIM ≥ 0.92, edge correlation ≥ 0.8, paint IoU ≥ 0.95 and at most 380 strokes.** `final_reward` = max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (scaled by 380 / strokes above 380). Reported as well: the mean ΔE after a 4 mm blur, the SSIM at a 0.5 mm blur, and per colour region of the picture (the connected areas nearest to one paint, at least 30 mm²) the fraction within ΔE 10: the minimum and the area-weighted mean. `s.score()` returns exactly these metrics for the current sheet: a scoring service (a separate container) replays the actions you have executed since your last `s.reset()` and scores the resulting sheet.
text.SCORE_L:
- Before scoring, the main sheet is aligned with the picture: your painting is moved by the single translation (no rotation or scaling, one shift for the whole sheet, whole pixels up to 5 mm along each axis) that best matches the picture; every quantity below is taken after that shift, which is reported (`register_dx_mm`, `register_dy_mm`). If the best match lies at the 5 mm limit, no shift is applied.
- The grader compares the main sheet with the picture: both blurred (σ = 1 mm); **ΔE** = the CIELAB colour difference (ΔE*ab) per pixel over the region where either has paint (dilated by 2 mm): its mean and 90th percentile; **SSIM** of the lightness L* (σ 1.5 mm windows); **edge correlation** = the correlation of the lightness-gradient magnitudes of the two blurred pictures over that region; **paint IoU** of the painted areas (paint coverage ≥ 0.5); the **number of strokes** on the main sheet (painted contacts). **Success iff, after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, mean ΔE ≤ 2.0, p90 ΔE ≤ 6.0, SSIM ≥ 0.92, edge correlation ≥ 0.8, paint IoU ≥ 0.95 and at most 380 strokes** (the recorded episode is replayed twice and both replays must agree). The continuous score is max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (scaled by 380 / strokes above 380). Reported as well: the mean ΔE after a 4 mm blur, the SSIM at a 0.5 mm blur, and per colour region of the picture (the connected areas nearest to one paint, at least 30 mm²) the fraction within ΔE 10: the minimum and the area-weighted mean.
text.SRC: The exemplar is this robot's painting after Utagawa Hiroshige, *Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake* (1857), a public-domain work (Wikimedia Commons `File:Hiroshige, Sudden shower over Shin-Ōhashi bridge and Atake, 1857.jpg`, Public domain); the exemplar picture is CC0
text.DESC_TOML_U: RoboPaint acrylic stroke copy: embodied robotic painting (ManiSkill 3.0.1 Franka Panda with a round acrylic brush; the paint is libmypaint 1.6.1 with the mypaint-brushes preset tanda/acrylic-03-paint, an opaque paint whose mark width follows the pressure): produce one replayable trajectory that copies the painting shown in the picture target.png (a small acrylic painting after Utagawa Hiroshige's woodblock print Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake, 1857) onto the main sheet with 10 premixed paints, in at most 380 strokes. Scored at a 1 mm scale against the picture after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis (success iff mean CIELAB ΔE <= 2.0, p90 ΔE <= 6.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.92, edge correlation >= 0.8, paint IoU >= 0.95 and at most 380 strokes; 1 - mean ΔE / 20 is the continuous score). s.score() is served by a separate scoring container.
text.DESC_TOML_L: RoboPaint acrylic stroke copy, STANDARD MODE (robot as a service, eai-standard/2.2): embodied robotic acrylic painting (ManiSkill 3.0.1 Franka Panda with a round acrylic brush; libmypaint 1.6.1 paints) on the same frozen instance as the privileged task: copy the painting shown in the picture target.png (a small acrylic painting after Utagawa Hiroshige's woodblock print Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake, 1857) onto the main sheet in at most 380 strokes, with 10 premixed paints and a practice sheet for test strokes. The agent only gets a client: get_obs (camera RGB + proprioception), submit (ee_pose or joint_position chunks). No reset, no sheet readout, no brush model, no score; the sim service records the episode, which is replayed twice and scored at a 1 mm scale against the picture after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis (success iff mean CIELAB ΔE <= 2.0, p90 ΔE <= 6.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.92, edge correlation >= 0.8, paint IoU >= 0.95 and at most 380 strokes).

text.README_INSTANCE: copy the painting in `environment/target.png` (a small acrylic painting after Utagawa Hiroshige's woodblock print Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake, 1857; the exemplar = this robot's painting of a hidden program of 292 strokes in 4 layers made by our stroke-based painting optimiser from the public-domain source) onto the 227 mm main sheet in at most 380 strokes, with 10 premixed paints on a plate and a practice sheet beside it; the brush starts dry; start pose = PandaStick's rest keyframe; everything frozen in `environment/instance.json` (the brush preset's text included)
text.GOAL_MD: Copy the painting (笔触临摹): after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, mean CIELAB ΔE <= 2.0, p90 ΔE <= 6.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.92, edge correlation >= 0.8, paint IoU >= 0.95 and at most 380 strokes. `final_reward` = max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (× 380 / strokes above 380).
text.DIFF_MD: The exemplar is layered (a ground of 16 mm strokes, forms at 9 mm, details at 5 mm and 3 mm) and the paint is opaque, so later strokes hide earlier ones and the picture shows the strokes themselves. Measured on the robot with this task's grader (after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis): the whole program shifted by 2-4 mm (five offsets) passes (the worst: ΔE 0.73 / p90 1.7 / SSIM 0.977 / edge 0.96); the program at twice the speed passes (ΔE 1.15 / p90 2.9 / SSIM 0.958 / edge 0.92); these fail: the naive palette hatching (ΔE 16.93 / p90 42.3 / SSIM 0.175 / edge 0.08); the naive sheet-covering rows (ΔE 7.12 / p90 18.7 / SSIM 0.618 / edge 0.13); the program with its layers reversed (ΔE 6.29 / p90 21.5 / SSIM 0.762 / edge 0.49); a coarse-brush-only painting (16 + 9 mm brushes, the whole budget) (ΔE 6.29 / p90 16.9 / SSIM 0.628 / edge 0.17); the two most used paints swapped (ΔE 2.39 / p90 12.9 / SSIM 0.929 / edge 0.93); 20 % more press (ΔE 3.28 / p90 9.9 / SSIM 0.796 / edge 0.60). The oracle reproduces the exemplar (ΔE 0.14).
text.REF_MD: The exemplar IS the robot's execution of the hidden stroke program (`solution/program.json`, `solution/ref_oil.py`: a dip whenever the paint changes, travel, touch-down, the Catmull-Rom path at its speed with the press interpolated, lift; lag feed-forward), so the oracle reproduces it exactly. The program comes from our stroke-based painting optimiser (layered coarse-to-fine greedy strokes with libmypaint in the loop, `solution/README.md`). The plan is frozen at generation time (`solution/oracle_qpos.npy`); `solution/solve.sh` replays it:
text.L_ORACLE: `solution/`: streams the privileged oracle's joint targets (one row per control step, `hold`) as `joint_position` chunks; the recorded trajectory then equals the privileged oracle's
